messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: OrbitHealth SDK & resilience checklist (next steps)

Hi Sanjay & Lindsey,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great session and appreciated the clarity on the telemetry and latency targets for your clinician-facing search flows. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the integration / architecture items we agreed to follow up on and call out a resilience checklist specific to your high-concurrency embedding + reranker path.

Top-line next steps (proposed):
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/engineering team (ben/marcus from our side) to walk SDK auth and routing patterns.
- Share a short sample prompt set + expected structured output examples for the reranker and tool-calling use case.
- Confirm quotas and request-id expectations (how OrbitHealth will surface request IDs and what you'd like Redwood to log/echo).
- Provide a resilience runbook draft (429 handling, retry/backoff, idempotency guidance) — attached a starting SLA skeleton and PoC requirements.

Integration items to validate on the call:
1) SDK setup & auth: API key flow vs. mTLS for Private deployment; brief steps for rotating keys and recommended header (x-request-id) usage.
2) Routing & model selection: preferred latency vs. cost policy; how to pin reranker model vs. fall back to cheaper embed-only path.
3) Structured output / tool-calling: expected JSON schema, error handling semantics when tools fail mid-call.
4) Embeddings + reranker pipeline: embedding batch sizes, near-real-time vs. offline indexing, similarity thresholds you care about.

Resilience checklist (quick):
- Surface x-request-id on every response and require clients to send it (idempotency and support correlation).
- Client-side: exponential backoff with jitter for 429s, circuit-breaker after configurable failure threshold.
- Server-side: recommend idempotency key header for mutation-like calls; for read-only generation, use deterministic request-id to deduplicate replays.
- Quotas: clarify soft limits (per-minute) and hard throttles (429). We'll propose a burst policy for your initial ramp.

Please let me know 2–3 times that work this week for the technical deep-dive. I attached the SLA draft and your PoC checklist so your procurement and infra teams can start review.

Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Aisha,

Thanks — that summary is helpful. Lindsey and I reviewed the attachments and have a few clarifying questions before we lock a time with our infra crew: 

1) For the idempotency guidance: our primary concern is de-duplicating retries coming from mobile clients where network blips can cause double-submits. Does Redwood recommend a specific idempotency header name or generation pattern? Will Redwood surface the server-side decision if a request was deduped (so our client can reconcile)?

2) On quotas: we need a clear escalation path if we hit sustained 429s during a pilot. Procurement will want to see the SLA itemized and an emergency contact for priority bursts.

3) For embeddings throughput: is there an example config for batching and the expected latency impact for batches of ~256 tokens? We want to understand the trade-offs so our indexing pipeline can be tuned.

Happy to take a 60-minute slot Wed or Thu — tentative preference Wed 11/11 10:00am PT. Looping in procurement separately for contract items.

Best,
Sanjay
CTO, OrbitHealth

Quick responses (will expand into short docs + a slide for the call):

1) Idempotency recommendation:
- Header name: Idempotency-Key (we already support this in SDKs).
- Generation: client: UUIDv4; mobile SDK helper persists key for retry window of 5 minutes for interactive flows. For background jobs, include deterministic id (job_id + sequence).
- Server response: when a duplicate is detected we return 200/202 with header X-Redwood-Dedupe: true and X-Redwood-Original-Request-Id: <original-request-id>. We also echo back the x-request-id if provided.

2) 429 & burst policy (summary):
- Soft quota: per-minute token units with 2x burst for 10 seconds. Soft breaches return 429 with Retry-After header and a sub-code (429.BURST) indicating burst enforcement.
- Hard quota: sustained exceedance > 2 minutes triggers 429.HARD and optional request blocking until quota is increased.
- Emergency escalation: dedicated partner slack + on-call pager for Enterprise pilots (contact provided on contract). For now we'll include a dedicated escalation alias (partners-pilot@redwood.com) in the SLA draft.

3) Embeddings throughput (preview):
- Batch size guidance: 16 -> lowest latency (best for real-time); 64 -> tradeoff; 256 -> highest throughput but expect higher tail latency. For your dataset, 256 batching for background indexing is recommended; for interactive query-time embedding use 16–32.
- Expected per-batch token overhead: ~8–12ms per token on our quantized runtime (numbers vary by model). We'll include concrete numbers in the doc for the model you picked.

I'll prepare two artifacts by EOD: a one-pager idempotency + 429 runbook and a short slide for the Wed call. Marcus/Evelyn, if you can drop your slides into the shared drive link, I'll stitch together.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
